mainTopic: Burning doubtful and impure תרומה together: conflicting reports of רבי יהושע, indirect versus direct impurity, and when a big loss allows an exception.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: only food, not other כלים, becomes impure from the airspace of a כלי חרס. The גמרא then asks whether רבי יהושע really allowed burning doubtful (תלויה) תרומה together with impure (טמאה) תרומה on ערב פסח, since a תוספתא of רבי יוסי seems to forbid it. רב חסדא answers that רבי שמעון and רבי יוסי report רבי יהושע's view differently, and he proves this from a ברייתא. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא raises a similar contradiction from a barrel of doubtful תרומה, where רבי יהושע allows only indirect causing of impurity (גרמא), not direct action (בידים). He gives the same answer. רבי אלעזר then shows that רבי יהושע does allow direct action when a barrel of תרומה wine breaks above impure חולין. He explains that this is because of the loss of חולין, and אביי adds that only a big loss counts. The גמרא proves this from a parallel case of oil, and explains why new wine is a big loss: aging it risks a mishap (תקלה), and wine for sprinkling cannot be stored in a disgusting container. Finally, a ברייתא shows that the worry about a mishap is itself a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי tries to decide between them, and the others' reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only food becomes impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its proof from the closeness of two פסוקים: only food is made impure by the אויר of a כלי חרס, not other כלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Whatever is inside it shall be impure,' and right next to it: 'From all the food.' This teaches that food becomes impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel, but other vessels do not become impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof from a ברייתא it started quoting on the previous amud. The ברייתא reads two neighboring פסוקים together to limit who becomes impure inside a כלי חרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק sounds like everything inside becomes impure. The next פסוק says 'food,' and the closeness (סמיכות) limits the rule to food only. This shows that the כלי חרס is not treated as if it were filled with שרץ. If it were, the vessels inside would also become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches' – introduces a source from a פסוק
It is placed right next to it (a lesson from neighboring verses)
The airspace inside an earthenware vessel

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי חרס makes food inside it impure through its airspace, but not other vessels. So the vessel is not treated as 'full of the שרץ.'

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Whatever is in it shall be impure,"
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from ויקרא יא:לג.

phrases.english: and juxtaposed to it: "From all the food."
phrases.notes: This is the very next פסוק, ויקרא יא:לד.

phrases.english: Food becomes impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין כׇּל הַכֵּלִים מִטַּמְּאִין מֵאֲוִיר כְּלִי חֶרֶס.
phrases.english: but not all vessels become impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: כֹּל אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֹכוֹ יִטְמָא, וּסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ: מִכׇּל הָאֹכֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא quoted earlier as proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a כלי חרס is not treated as filled with the שרץ, so it does not make vessels inside it impure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סמיכות of ויקרא יא:לג to יא:לד ('whatever is inside it' next to 'from all the food').

steps.title: רב חסדא asks: did רבי יהושע really allow burning both together?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא raises his own contradiction between two sources about פסח. He opens by asking whether רבי יהושע really said that doubtful and definitely impure תרומה may be burned together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא pointed out a contradiction between one teaching about פסח and another teaching about פסח, and he resolved it himself. Did רבי יהושע really say that both may be burned as one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. This line sets up a contradiction: רב חסדא questions whether רבי יהושע truly allowed burning תלויה and טמאה together on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יהושע allows burning doubtful (תלויה) תרומה together with definitely impure תרומה. רב חסדא's question warns us that another source seems to say רבי יהושע held the opposite. The question is a setup; the opposing source comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction (set two sources against each other)
A source about פסח against another source about פסח

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is both asking and answering. Here he is only setting up the problem. His resolution comes later.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda raised a contradiction
between Passover and Passover, and he resolved it:
Did Rabbi Yehoshua really say
that both of them are burned as one?
phrases.notes: Doubtful תרומה and definitely impure תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא רָמֵי פִּיסְחָא אַפִּיסְחָא וּמְשַׁנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of אויר כלי חרס and opens a new contradiction about burning תרומה on ערב פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's ruling in the משנה that תלויה and טמאה may be burned together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source (about to be quoted) seems to show that רבי יהושע did not allow burning them together.

steps.title: The contradicting source: רבי יוסי says the case being learned does not match the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the תוספתא it will contrast with our משנה. In it, רבי יוסי says the case derived does not match the source cited as proof, and asks what the earlier Sages actually testified about.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he contrasted it with this source: רבי יוסי said: The case being learned is not similar to the proof. When our Rabbis testified, what did they testify about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the contradicting source. רבי יוסי is beginning to argue with רבי מאיר's proof, and this line sets up his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר had argued that the testimonies of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים and רבי עקיבא prove that pure and impure items may be burned together. רבי יוסי says the comparison does not work. He will now go through each testimony to show it is different.

keyTerms.meaning: And contrast them with (introduces a contradicting source)
The case being learned is not similar to the proof

phrases.english: And he contrasted it: Rabbi Yosei said:
The case being derived is not similar to the proof;
when our Rabbis testified,
about what did they testify?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֵין הַנִּדּוֹן דּוֹמֶה לִרְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that sets up the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's ruling allowing burning both together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תוספתא of רבי יוסי (continued next) will show רבי יהושע forbidding it.

steps.title: First testimony: both pieces of meat were already impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי explains the first testimony. Meat impure from a ולד הטומאה may be burned with meat impure from an אב הטומאה, because both are already impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they testified about meat that became impure from a secondary source of impurity, that we burn it together with meat that became impure from a primary source of impurity, then this one is impure and that one is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי shows that the first testimony involves two items that are both already impure. So it cannot prove we may burn something pure with something impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning them together only raises the level of impurity of the lighter piece. It does not ruin anything that was still pure. That is very different from burning pure תרומה with impure תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: A secondary source of impurity (something made impure by an אב הטומאה)
This one is impure and that one is impure

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַל הַבָּשָׂר שֶׁנִּטְמָא בִּוְלַד הַטּוּמְאָה
phrases.english: If about meat that became impure through a secondary source of impurity,
that we burn it
together with meat that became impure through a primary source of impurity,
this one is impure and that one is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם עַל הַבָּשָׂר שֶׁנִּטְמָא בִּוְלַד הַטּוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's question 'what did they testify about?' for the first testimony.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי מאיר's proof from רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים's testimony about meat.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both pieces of meat were already impure, so nothing pure was ruined.

steps.title: Second testimony: the oil was already disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי explains the second testimony. Oil made פסול by a טבול יום may be lit in a lamp made impure by a טמא מת, because the oil was already unusable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they testified about oil that was disqualified by a טבול יום, that we light it in a lamp that became impure through someone impure from a corpse, then this one is disqualified and that one is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי shows that רבי עקיבא's testimony also involves no pure item. The oil was already פסול before it touched the impure lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסול oil cannot be used as תרומה anyway, so making it טמא causes no real loss. Again, nothing pure is being ruined, so this cannot prove that pure and impure may be burned together.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who immersed today and is pure only after nightfall; he makes תרומה פסול
Disqualified (unusable, but not able to spread impurity)
A person who became impure from a corpse

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁנִּפְסַל בִּטְבוּל יוֹם,
phrases.english: If about oil that was disqualified by a tevul yom,
that we light it
in a lamp that became impure through one impure from a corpse,
this one is disqualified and that one is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁנִּפְסַל בִּטְבוּל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 4, now for רבי עקיבא's testimony.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי מאיר's proof from רבי עקיבא's testimony about oil.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The oil was already פסול, so no usable item was lost.

steps.title: רבי יוסי agrees: two kinds of impure תרומה may be burned together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי concedes that תרומה impure from a ולד הטומאה may be burned with תרומה impure from an אב הטומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We too agree regarding תרומה that became impure from a secondary source of impurity, that we may burn it with תרומה that became impure from a primary source of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי states what he does accept. Following the testimonies, two impure items may be burned together even if one becomes more impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This draws the exact line of the testimonies. Raising the level of something already impure is allowed. This sets up his next point: the real problem is ruining something that might still be pure.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן; it must be kept pure

phrases.english: We too agree regarding teruma
that became impure through a secondary source of impurity,
that we burn it together with teruma
that became impure through a primary source of impurity,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אָנוּ מוֹדִים בִּתְרוּמָה שֶׁנִּטְמֵאת בִּוְלַד הַטּוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the lesson of the two testimonies to תרומה and states what רבי יוסי concedes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure תרומה of a lower level may be burned with impure תרומה of a higher level.

steps.title: But doubtful תרומה may not be burned with impure תרומה, because אליהו might declare it pure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי refuses to allow burning תלויה together with טמאה, because אליהו might come and declare the doubtful תרומה pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how can we burn even doubtful תרומה together with impure תרומה? Perhaps אליהו will come and declare them pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי draws his line. Doubtful תרומה is not like impure תרומה, so it may not be burned together with definitely impure תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תלויה might really be pure. אליהו הנביא could one day clarify its status and declare it pure. Burning it with impure תרומה would make it definitely impure, causing a loss the testimonies never allowed. This statement prepares the contradiction with רבי יהושע, which the next passage will complete.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Hanging' – תרומה whose purity is in doubt
Perhaps אליהו will come (and settle the doubt)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not saying תלויה is pure. It is a real doubt, so it is not treated like definitely impure תרומה. Only its unclear status keeps us from ruining it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the key distinction for the sugya: impure with impure is allowed, but doubtful with impure is not. רב חסדא's contradiction with רבי יהושע depends on it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי: two impure items may be burned together. Doubtful (תלויה) תרומה may not be burned with impure תרומה, because אליהו might declare it pure.

phrases.english: But how can we burn
even teruma in doubt together with impure teruma?
Perhaps Elijah will come and declare them pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הֵיאַךְ נִשְׂרוֹף אֲפִילּוּ תְּלוּיָה עִם הַטְּמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 6: impure with impure is allowed, but doubtful with impure is not.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Extending the permission to burning תלויה together with טמאה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: תלויה may yet be declared pure, so making it definitely impure is a real loss.

steps.title: Two תנאים report רבי יהושע's view differently
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא resolves the contradiction. One source is רבי שמעון's version of רבי יהושע, and the other is רבי יוסי's version of רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he resolved it: This source is רבי שמעון's report of רבי יהושע's opinion. That source is רבי יוסי's report of רבי יהושע's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction it raised earlier. The two sources do not truly clash. They are two different reports of what רבי יהושע held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One source says that, according to רבי יהושע, תלויה and טמאה may be burned together. The other, which we just saw from רבי יוסי, says they may not. רב חסדא explains that רבי שמעון reports רבי יהושע as lenient, while רבי יוסי reports him as strict, so this is a dispute between תנאים about what רבי יהושע said.

keyTerms.meaning: And he resolved it (answering a contradiction)
This one ... that one (assigning each source to a different view)

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions are described as 'according to רבי יהושע.' The disagreement is not about whose view to follow. It is about what רבי יהושע actually said, as reported by רבי שמעון versus רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: And he resolved: This is Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: The source that permits burning תלויה with טמאה.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yehoshua.
That is Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: The source that forbids burning them together.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁנֵּי: הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between רבי יוסי's strict report (steps 3-7) and the other source's lenient report of רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each source to a different תנא who reports the same master differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two sources about רבי יהושע's view directly contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון reports רבי יהושע as lenient about burning תלויה with טמאה. רבי יוסי reports him as strict.

steps.title: The ברייתא: burning תרומה before שבת on ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. When the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת, רבי מאיר says all kinds of תרומה are burned together, and רבי יוסי says each kind is burned separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: When the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת, we remove all the חמץ before שבת. We burn impure, doubtful, and pure תרומה together. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי says: Pure by itself, doubtful by itself, and impure by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the source for the dispute it just mentioned. This first part of the ברייתא gives the views of רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חמץ cannot be burned on שבת, so it must be burned on Friday. On Friday some of it could still be eaten, so the question is whether all the תרומה may be thrown into one fire. רבי מאיר allows all three kinds together. רבי יוסי insists on three separate fires so that no possibly-pure תרומה is made impure by contact.

keyTerms.meaning: The fourteenth of ניסן that falls on שבת

phrases.english: As it was taught: The fourteenth (of Nisan)
that falls on Shabbat,
we remove everything before Shabbat,
phrases.notes: Burning is not allowed on שבת itself.

phrases.english: and we burn terumah:
impure, in doubt, and pure (all together),
the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei says:
pure by itself,
and in-doubt by itself,
and impure by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cites the source behind רב חסדא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That the תנאים disagree about burning different kinds of תרומה together
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about ערב פסח that falls on שבת

steps.title: רבי שמעון's report of the רבי אליעזר–רבי יהושע dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argued only about burning תלויה with טמאה. רבי אליעזר says separately and רבי יהושע says together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע did not argue about pure and impure תרומה; both agree these are not burned together. They also did not argue about doubtful and pure; both agree these are burned together. What did they argue about? Doubtful and impure. רבי אליעזר says: burn each by itself. רבי יהושע says: both together.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון's account of the earlier dispute. This is the lenient report of רבי יהושע that רב חסדא mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון lays out three pairs. Pure with impure is forbidden by all. Doubtful with pure is permitted by all. Doubtful with impure is the only real argument. This shows that רבי שמעון's רבי יהושע is the lenient one.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון: pure with impure is never burned together, doubtful with pure is always allowed, and only doubtful with impure is disputed. רבי יהושע permits that pair.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua did not disagree
about the pure and the impure,
that we do not burn (them together),
(nor) about the in-doubt and the pure,
that we do burn (them together).
About what did they disagree?
About the in-doubt and the impure,
for Rabbi Eliezer says:
this one should be burned by itself
and that one by itself.
And Rabbi Yehoshua says:
both of them together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and supplies the lenient report of רבי יהושע.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון reports רבי יהושע as permitting תלויה with טמאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's statement in the ברייתא

steps.title: Isn't our משנה said by רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רב חסדא's answer. Our משנה, which reports רבי יהושע as allowing תלויה and טמאה to be burned together, is said by רבי יוסי himself. So how can רב חסדא call רבי יוסי's version of רבי יהושע the strict one?
steps.simpleTranslation: But our משנה is רבי יוסי's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge to the picture it just drew. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יוסי is the one who says that רבי יהושע allows burning תלויה and טמאה together. רב חסדא just assigned that lenient report to רבי שמעון and the strict one to רבי יוסי. So how can רבי יוסי be the strict reporter when he states the lenient view in the משנה?

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (where רבי יוסי reports רבי יהושע's view)

phrases.english: But our Mishnah
is Rabbi Yosei's!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how רבי שמעון's report relates to רבי יוסי's ruling in the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's resolution (step 8) that רבי יוסי reports רבי יהושע as strict
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה, רבי יוסי himself reports רבי יהושע as saying 'שתיהן כאחת', so רבי יוסי cannot be the source of the strict version.

steps.title: רבי יוסי argues against רבי מאיר using רבי שמעון's report
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי is telling רבי מאיר that even the most lenient report of רבי יהושע, רבי שמעון's, never allows burning pure with impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי יוסי is saying to רבי מאיר: Even רבי שמעון's version of רבי יהושע, who is lenient, is lenient only with doubtful and impure. With pure and impure, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי יוסי is using רבי שמעון's lenient report as an argument against רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יוסי is not giving his own version of רבי יהושע. He is arguing with רבי מאיר, who let pure and impure תרומה burn together. He quotes רבי שמעון's lenient version only to show that even it forbids pure with impure, so רבי מאיר's rule has no support.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is saying

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר stands alone in allowing pure and impure תרומה to burn together. Even רבי שמעון's lenient רבי יהושע forbids it, and that is רבי יוסי's argument.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that burning pure תרומה with impure תרומה is the line almost every view refuses to cross. Only רבי מאיר permits it.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yosei is saying to Rabbi Meir:
Even Rabbi Shimon
according to Rabbi Yehoshua, who is lenient,
when he is lenient, it is with in-doubt and impure,
but with pure and impure — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the statement as an argument aimed at an opponent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יוסי in the משנה reports רבי יהושע as lenient, רבי יוסי seems to hold the lenient version, which contradicts רב חסדא's answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the משנה, רבי יוסי is not giving his own version of רבי יהושע. He quotes רבי שמעון's lenient version as an argument against רבי מאיר, showing that even that version forbids burning pure with impure. So רב חסדא's answer stands.

steps.title: רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא raises a contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא set a תרומה law against a פסח law and resolved it himself. It then asks whether רבי יהושע really said both may be burned together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא pointed out a contradiction between a law about תרומה and a law about פסח, and he answered it himself. The question was: did רבי יהושע really say that both may be burned together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that another אמורא, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, noticed the same kind of contradiction about רבי יהושע. Here it opens the challenge by asking whether רבי יהושע really allowed burning doubtful and impure תרומה together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'פסח law' is the ruling in our משנה about burning תרומה on ערב פסח, where רבי יהושע allows burning תלויה (doubtful תרומה) together with טמאה (impure תרומה). That ruling seems to let a person make doubtful תרומה impure directly. The words 'מי אמר' signal surprise and set up the contradicting source that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction (literally 'he threw' one source against another)
פסח; here, the law about burning תרומה on ערב פסח
Both together (burning doubtful and impure תרומה in one fire)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina
contrasted a law of teruma with a law of Pesach,
and he resolved it:
phrases.notes: He both asked and answered on his own.

phrases.english: Did Rabbi Yehoshua actually say
that both are burned together?
phrases.notes: Doubtful תרומה together with impure תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא רָמֵי תְּרוּמָה אַפִּיסְחָא, וּמְשַׁנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a parallel contradiction and resolution, similar to רב חסדא's in step 8, now told in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's ruling that doubtful and impure תרומה may be burned together on ערב פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Burning them together makes doubtful תרומה impure directly. The contradicting source, about to be quoted, suggests רבי יהושע forbids that.

steps.title: The barrel of תרומה with a doubt of impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about a barrel of תרומה with a doubt of impurity. רבי אליעזר says to protect it. רבי יהושע says one may leave it exposed, in an unprotected place or uncovered.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contrasted it with this משנה. A barrel of תרומה developed a doubt of טומאה. רבי אליעזר says: if it was sitting in an exposed place, move it to a hidden place, and if it was uncovered, cover it. רבי יהושע says: if it was in a hidden place, he may move it to an exposed place, and if it was covered, he may uncover it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that will contradict the ערב פסח ruling. In this משנה, רבי יהושע allows exposing doubtful תרומה so it may become impure on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תרומה is only doubtfully impure, רבי אליעזר wants it guarded. רבי יהושע says there is no need to guard it, so a person may even put it where it will likely become impure. Notice what רבי יהושע allows here: only setting things up so impurity may happen. He says nothing about making it impure with one's own hands.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it with (introduces a contradicting source)
An exposed, vulnerable place where impurity is likely

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע is not telling a person to make the תרומה impure himself. He only allows leaving it unprotected so it may become impure on its own. That difference is the whole point of the next step.

phrases.english: And they contrasted it with:
A barrel of teruma
in which a doubt of impurity arose,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
If it was resting in an exposed place,
he should put it in a hidden place,
and if it was uncovered, he should cover it.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
If it was resting in a hidden place,
he may put it in an exposed place,
and if it was covered, he may uncover it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ: חָבִית שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד בָּהּ סְפֵק טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the contradicting source for the question in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: Showing that רבי יהושע's leniency in the barrel case is limited to indirect exposure
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה about a barrel of תרומה with a doubt of impurity (תרומות ח)

steps.title: Indirect causing is allowed, direct action is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from the משנה: רבי יהושע allows causing impurity indirectly but not with one's hands. That clashes with burning doubtful and impure תרומה together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Causing it indirectly, yes. With one's hands, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the contradiction. In the barrel case רבי יהושע only allowed indirect causing of impurity, so he must forbid making the תרומה impure directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the barrel in an exposed place is only גרמא, an indirect cause. Burning doubtful תרומה together with impure תרומה makes it impure בידים, by direct action. So how could רבי יהושע allow that on ערב פסח?

keyTerms.meaning: Indirect causation; setting up a situation that leads to a result

steps.whyThisMatters: The line between גרמא and בידים runs through the rest of this סוגיא, including רבי אלעזר's contradiction that comes next.

phrases.english: Indirect causation, yes;
with one's hands, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּרָמָא — אִין, בְּיָדַיִם — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the barrel משנה that creates the contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ערב פסח ruling of רבי יהושע allowing doubtful and impure תרומה to be burned together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The barrel משנה implies רבי יהושע forbids making doubtful תרומה impure directly. Burning it with impure תרומה is exactly that.

steps.title: Two different reports of רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers that the ערב פסח source follows רבי שמעון's version of רבי יהושע. The barrel source follows רבי יוסי's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he resolved it: this source is רבי שמעון's version of רבי יהושע, and that source is רבי יוסי's version of רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers his own contradiction. He says the two sources come from two different תנאים, each reporting רבי יהושע's view differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי שמעון's version, רבי יהושע allows burning תלויה with טמאה together, even though that is direct action. In רבי יוסי's version, רבי יהושע never allows making doubtful תרומה impure directly, only indirectly. So the contradiction is between two reporters, not inside רבי יהושע's own view.

keyTerms.meaning: This one ... that one (assigning each source to a different authority)

steps.whatToRemember: Burning together on ערב פסח is רבי שמעון's report of רבי יהושע. Allowing only indirect exposure is רבי יוסי's report of רבי יהושע. This is the same answer רב חסדא gave in step 8.

phrases.english: And he resolved it:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: this is Rabbi Shimon's version of Rabbi Yehoshua,
phrases.notes: He means the ערב פסח ruling, where both are burned together.

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: that is Rabbi Yosei's version of Rabbi Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: He means the ruling about the barrel, where you may only make it impure indirectly.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁנֵּי: הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in steps 13 to 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different תנאים (תנאי נינהו)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources reflect one single view of רבי יהושע, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון and רבי יוסי report רבי יהושע differently, so each source matches its own reporter.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר raises a contradiction between two תרומה laws
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רבי אלעזר contrasted one תרומה law with another and resolved it himself. It asks whether רבי יהושע really said that indirect causing is allowed but direct action is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר pointed out a contradiction between one law of תרומה and another law of תרומה, and he answered it himself. The question was: did רבי יהושע really say that indirect causing is allowed, but direct action with one's hands is not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new contradiction, this time from רבי אלעזר. It is setting up the next move: a second תרומה source will be quoted to test the rule just drawn from the barrel משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the rule itself is being questioned: is רבי יהושע really strict about direct action? The barrel משנה (step 14) is the first תרומה source. Another תרומה source, about to be quoted, will seem to show רבי יהושע taking a different position.

keyTerms.meaning: A law of תרומה against another law of תרומה

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar
contrasted a law of teruma with another law of teruma,
and he resolved it:
Did Rabbi Yehoshua actually say
indirect causation, yes, but with one's hands, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר רָמֵי תְּרוּמָה אַתְּרוּמָה, וּמְשַׁנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new contradiction aimed at the גרמא versus בידים rule drawn in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that רבי יהושע allows only גרמא and forbids making doubtful תרומה impure בידים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another תרומה source, about to be quoted, will seem to conflict with this distinction in רבי יהושע's name.

steps.title: The broken barrel of תרומה above impure wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings a משנה about a barrel of תרומה that broke in the upper part of a winepress, with impure חולין wine below. רבי אליעזר agrees that a רביעית should be saved in purity if possible. If not, he says to let it flow down and become impure, but not to make it impure by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he raised a contradiction: A barrel of תרומה wine broke in the upper part of a winepress, and below it is impure ordinary wine. רבי אליעזר agrees with רבי יהושע that if a person can save a רביעית of it in purity, he should save it. If not, רבי אליעזר says: let it go down and become impure, but he should not make it impure with his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the contradiction that step 17 announced. It quotes the case and רבי אליעזר's view first, so we can then hear רבי יהושע's surprising view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the pure תרומה flows into the impure חולין below, the תרומה becomes impure. The whole mixture then gets the status of impure תרומה, which nobody may drink. רבי אליעזר keeps the same position he has held all along: let it become impure on its own, but do not actively make it impure.

keyTerms.meaning: And he raised a contradiction: setting one source against another
Winepress (it had an upper part and a lower part)
A quarter-לוג, a small liquid measure
In a state of ritual purity

steps.confusionAlert: The upper wine is the holy תרומה. The lower wine is the ordinary חולין, and it is already impure. The danger is the pure תרומה falling down into the impure ordinary wine.

phrases.english: And he raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר is now quoting the second source mentioned in step 17.

phrases.english: A barrel of teruma that broke
in the upper press
phrases.notes: This is the upper area of the winepress, where the grapes are pressed.

phrases.english: and beneath it is impure non-sacred wine —
Rabbi Eliezer concedes to Rabbi Yehoshua
that if he is able to rescue from it
a quarter-log in purity, he should rescue it,
phrases.notes: For example, by catching it in a pure vessel.

phrases.english: and if not —
phrases.notes: For example, if only impure vessels are available.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: let it descend and become impure,
but he should not make it impure with his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ: חָבִית שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בַּגַּת הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the contradicting source that step 17 announced.
steps.raayaObject: What רבי יהושע holds about directly making pure תרומה impure
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the broken barrel in the upper winepress (תרומות פרק ח)

steps.title: רבי יהושע allows making it impure by hand
steps.stepSummary: In the same משנה, רבי יהושע says one may make the תרומה impure with his own hand. This contradicts the earlier inference that רבי יהושע forbids direct action.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: he may make it impure with his hand!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punch line of the contradiction. רבי יהושע here allows direct action, even though step 15 inferred that he only allows indirect causing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier barrel case, רבי יהושע only allowed leaving the תרומה exposed, which is indirect. From that, we learned he forbids making תרומה impure with one's hands. Here he openly permits it, for example by catching the wine in impure vessels or plugging the opening with an impure vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: He may make it impure with his hand (direct action)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: he may make it impure with his hand!
phrases.notes: That's surprising, because it clashes with what we figured out earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: יְטַמְּאֶנָּה בַּיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה and shows exactly where it clashes with step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that רבי יהושע allows only indirect causing of impurity, not direct action
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the broken barrel case, רבי יהושע explicitly allows making pure תרומה impure by hand. That directly contradicts the claim that he forbids direct action.

steps.title: Different because ordinary wine would be lost
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר resolves the contradiction himself. In the winepress case, the impure חולין below would be ruined. To prevent that loss, רבי יהושע allows even direct action.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he resolved it: There it is different, because there is a loss of ordinary wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers his own question by showing that the winepress case has a special factor that the other case does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תרומה falls into the חולין below, all the ordinary wine turns into a mixture with impure תרומה and becomes forbidden. That is a big loss. Because of this, רבי יהושע allows making the תרומה impure by hand to save the ordinary wine. Normally, though, he still forbids direct action.

keyTerms.meaning: And he resolved it (answered the contradiction)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהושע, the basic rule is that one may let תרומה become impure indirectly but not make it impure with one's hands. The exception is when doing so prevents a loss of חולין; then even direct action is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a general rule can have exceptions without being cancelled. The rule against direct action stays in place, and avoiding a financial loss of ordinary food is what allows the exception.

phrases.english: And he resolved it:
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר answers his own contradiction.

phrases.english: There it is different,
phrases.notes: "There" means the broken barrel in the winepress.

phrases.english: since there is a loss of non-sacred produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁנֵּי: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 18-19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the winepress case has a special factor, the loss of חולין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע seems to contradict himself, forbidding direct impurity in one case and allowing it in another.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהושע generally forbids direct impurity of תרומה. He allows it only when it prevents the loss of חולין.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה also involves a loss of wood
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that in our משנה, burning the doubtful (תלויה) תרומה in its own fire, apart from the impure (טמאה), also causes a loss, because extra wood is needed. So why doesn't רבי יוסי's version of רבי יהושע allow burning them together there?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged this: In our משנה too there is a loss, a loss of wood!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the answer from step 20. If preventing loss is enough to allow direct action, then the ערב פסח case should be allowed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said רבי יהושע permits direct action when there is a loss. In the ערב פסח case, burning the תלויה in a separate fire costs extra wood, which is also a loss. So the logic of step 20 seems to permit burning תלויה and טמאה together, yet רבי יוסי's version of רבי יהושע forbids it.

phrases.english: Rava objected to it:
In the Mishnah too there is a loss of wood!
phrases.notes: Burning the תלויה in its own fire, apart from the טמאה, needs extra wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the loss-based reasoning of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that loss justifies directly making תרומה impure (step 20).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If loss permits direct action, the wood loss in the ערב פסח case should also permit burning תלויה with טמאה, but in רבי יוסי's version of רבי יהושע it does not.

steps.title: אביי: only a big loss counts
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the Sages were concerned about a large loss, like ruining all the חולין. They were not concerned about a small loss, like a few pieces of wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The Sages were concerned about a big loss. They were not concerned about a small loss.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends step 20 by splitting losses into two sizes. Only a big loss is enough to allow direct action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The winepress case involves a big loss, since all the חולין wine would be ruined. The ערב פסח case involves only a little extra wood. So a small loss does not override the rule against making possibly-pure (תלויה) תרומה impure by hand.
steps.whyThisMatters: The distinction between a big loss and a small loss is a key principle across הלכה for when the Sages relax a rule.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
For a great loss, they were concerned;
for a small loss, they were not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction by degree (big loss vs. small loss)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any loss, even the cost of extra wood, should allow direct action.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a big loss allows it. Extra wood is a small loss and does not count.

steps.title: Asking for a source for the big-loss rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the Sages cared about a big loss but not about a small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say that they were concerned about a big loss but not about a small loss?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of אביי's distinction. This line sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's distinction makes sense, but the גמרא wants a source showing the Sages actually used it. The answer will come from a case where a small loss was not enough to permit direct action.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this?

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that for a great loss they were concerned,
and for a small loss they were not concerned?

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה (as the opening of the proof)
steps.triggerLanguage: ומְנָא תֵּימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for אביי's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the Sages distinguish between a big loss and a small loss.

steps.title: The barrel of oil: even רבי יהושע forbids direct action
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a barrel of תרומה oil broke in the upper press, with impure חולין below. Both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree that you save a רביעית in purity if you can. If you cannot, let it flow down, but do not make it impure by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: A barrel of תרומה oil broke in the upper press, and in the lower press there is impure חולין. רבי אליעזר agrees with רבי יהושע that if one can save a רביעית of it in purity, he should save it. If not, let it flow down and become impure, but he should not make it impure with his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the proof. This case looks just like the wine case, but because it is oil, even רבי יהושע forbids making it impure by hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the wine case of step 19, רבי יהושע allowed direct action because of the big loss. Here, with oil, he agrees it is forbidden. The גמרא will explain that the loss with oil is small, which supports אביי's rule.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'מודה רבי אליעזר לרבי יהושע' also appear in the wine case. There the agreement covers only saving a רביעית. The difference is what comes after: in the wine case רבי יהושע disagrees and allows making it impure by hand, but in the oil case no disagreement is recorded. So everyone, including רבי יהושע, forbids direct action with oil.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
A barrel of teruma oil
that broke in the upper press,
and in the lower press there is impure non-sacred produce:
Rabbi Eliezer concedes to Rabbi Yehoshua
that if he can rescue from it
a quarter-log in purity, he should rescue it;
and if not, let it go down and become impure,
but he should not make it impure by hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source requested in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule that a small loss does not allow direct action.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the broken barrel of תרומה oil.

steps.title: Why oil is different, and wine can be used too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that oil is a small loss because impure oil can still be burned for light. Then it challenges this: wine can also still be used, for sprinkling to make a nice smell.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about oil? That it is fit for lighting? Wine is also fit for sprinkling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first spells out why oil counts as a small loss. It then attacks this reasoning by showing that wine also has a use after becoming impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure oil is not fully wasted, since it can still be burned for light. That is why the loss is small and direct action is forbidden. But if wine can be sprinkled for fragrance, the wine case should also be a small loss, so why did רבי יהושע allow direct action there?

keyTerms.meaning: To light (burn as fuel for a lamp)
Sprinkling (wine sprayed for a pleasant smell)

phrases.english: What is different about oil?
That it is fit for lighting?
Wine too is fit for sprinkling!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the proof from step 24, then challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between oil (small loss) and wine (big loss).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If oil is a small loss because it can be used for light, wine should also be a small loss because it can be used for sprinkling.

steps.title: Sprinkling wine is valuable, says שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer that sprinkling is unimportant. שמואל, in the name of רבי חייא, teaches that wine for sprinkling is worth twice as much as wine for drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say sprinkling is not a real use, didn't שמואל say in the name of רבי חייא: We drink wine that costs a סלע per לוג, and we sprinkle wine that costs two סלעים per לוג!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its challenge. It rules out the easy answer that sprinkling doesn't count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could argue that sprinkling is too minor to count as using the wine. שמואל shows the opposite: sprinkling uses the finest, most expensive wine. So wine really does keep a meaningful use, and the challenge stands.

phrases.english: And if you will say
sprinkling is not a significant matter,
but didn't Shmuel say in the name of Rabbi Chiya:
One drinks from a log costing a sela,
and one sprinkles from a log costing two!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא זִילּוּף לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reinforces the challenge of step 25 by blocking an easy answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense that sprinkling is not a real use.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל shows sprinkling wine is worth more than drinking wine, so it is clearly a significant use.

steps.title: The wine case is about new wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the winepress case deals with new wine. New wine has no strong smell and is not good for sprinkling, so losing it really is a big loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is referring to new wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge with one word. The wine in the winepress is new, so it cannot be used for sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's teaching applies to aged, fragrant wine. Fresh wine in the press has no use once it becomes impure, so the loss is big and רבי יהושע allows direct action. Oil can always be used for light, so its loss is small, which proves אביי's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: The Sages relax the rule against making תרומה impure only for a big loss. New wine in a press has no use once impure, so it is a big loss. Oil can still be burned for light, so it is a small loss, just like the extra wood on ערב פסח.

phrases.english: With new wine.
phrases.notes: New wine lacks fragrance, so it is not used for sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחָדָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 25-26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Impure wine can be used for sprinkling, so its loss is small like oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is new wine, which is unfit for sprinkling, so its loss is big. אביי's distinction is proven.

steps.title: But the new wine can be aged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 27: even new wine is not lost, because you can age it until it is good for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it fit to be aged?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that new wine is a total loss. If you wait, the new wine becomes old wine, and old wine is good for sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said new wine is a big loss because it has no smell yet. This challenge says that is only true for now. If the impure תרומה wine is kept until it ages, it can still be used, so it should count as a small loss, just like oil.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
To age it (let it become old wine)

phrases.english: But isn't it fit to be aged?!
phrases.notes: Once aged, the wine would develop a smell and be usable for sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רָאוּי לְיַשְּׁנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 27, which said new wine is useless for sprinkling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that new impure wine is a total loss.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: New wine turns into old wine over time. So it can eventually be used for sprinkling and is not really lost.

steps.title: Keeping it may lead to a mishap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that keeping impure wine for a long time could lead to a mishap (תקלה). Someone might forget it is impure and drink it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may come through it to a mishap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why we do not tell him to age the wine. Keeping impure תרומה wine around for a long time is risky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the wine waits to age, people may forget that it is impure and drink it, which is forbidden. Because of this danger, the Sages treat the wine as if it cannot be kept. So it really is a big loss after all.

keyTerms.meaning: A mishap, a stumbling block (accidentally doing something forbidden)

phrases.english: He may come through it to a mishap.
phrases.notes: Over the long wait he might forget it is impure and drink it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָתֵי בֵּיהּ לִידֵי תַּקָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a new practical concern that blocks the suggestion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Aging the wine would save it, so it is a small loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: Aging is not allowed because of the risk of a mishap, so the wine is a real loss.
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the idea of תקלה, which drives the rest of this passage.

steps.title: Oil should carry the same risk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if keeping impure wine risks a mishap, keeping impure oil for burning should also risk a mishap.
steps.simpleTranslation: Oil too, he may come through it to a mishap!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the new answer against the oil case. People keep impure תרומה oil to burn for light, so someone could forget and eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said oil is only a small loss because it can be burned. But if we worry about a mishap with wine, we should also worry with oil. Then oil should also count as a big loss, and the proof from the oil case falls apart.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמֶן נָמֵי, אָתֵי בֵּיהּ לִידֵי תַּקָּלָה!
phrases.english: Oil too, he may come through it to a mishap!
phrases.notes: Impure oil kept for lighting might also be eaten by mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמֶן נָמֵי, אָתֵי בֵּיהּ לִידֵי תַּקָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer of Step 29 to the oil case, creating a new difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between oil (small loss) and wine (big loss).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mishap concern should apply equally to stored impure oil.

steps.title: Oil is kept in a disgusting container
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that impure oil is put in a disgusting container, so no one will come to eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he places it in a disgusting vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why oil is safe to keep. It is stored in a repulsive container that no one would eat from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil kept only for burning does not need to stay pleasant, so it can go into a disgusting container. That container is a reminder and keeps people from eating it. So there is no mishap with oil.

phrases.english: Because he places it in a disgusting vessel.
phrases.notes: People would not eat from such a container, so the oil will only be used for light.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרָמֵי לֵיהּ בִּכְלִי מָאוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a practical safeguard that exists for oil.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Oil carries the same mishap risk as wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Oil can be stored in a disgusting container, which removes the risk.

steps.title: Then put the wine in a disgusting container too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the same solution for wine: put it in a disgusting container while it ages.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wine too, he can place it in a disgusting vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we cannot use the same trick for wine. Store it in a repulsive container and let it age safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the disgusting container solves the problem for oil, it should solve it for wine too. Then aging the wine is safe, and it would again be a small loss.

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן נָמֵי, רָמֵי לֵיהּ בִּכְלִי מָאוּס!
phrases.english: Wine too, he can place it in a disgusting vessel!

steps.triggerLanguage: יַיִן נָמֵי, רָמֵי לֵיהּ בִּכְלִי מָאוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the oil solution from Step 31 and applies it to wine.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that wine cannot be safely kept.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The disgusting-container safeguard should work for wine as well.

steps.title: Wine for sprinkling cannot sit in a disgusting container
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Wine is kept for sprinkling because of its nice smell, and a disgusting container would ruin that.
steps.simpleTranslation: He wants it for sprinkling, and he will put it in a disgusting vessel?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the trick cannot work for wine. A disgusting container would spoil the very thing he wants the wine for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil is burned, so a bad container does not hurt it. Wine is sprinkled for a pleasant smell, and a repulsive container would make it smell bad. So wine has no safeguard, the mishap concern stands, and losing new wine remains a big loss.

keyTerms.meaning: For sprinkling (to make a pleasant smell)

steps.whatToRemember: Oil can be kept safely in a disgusting container because it is only burned. Wine for sprinkling cannot, so keeping it risks a mishap. That is why new wine counts as a big loss.

phrases.english: He wants it for sprinkling,
and he will put it in a disgusting vessel?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: of course not, it would ruin the smell.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְזִילּוּף קָא בָעֵי לֵיהּ, בִּכְלִי מָאוּס רָמֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 32.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying the disgusting-container solution to wine.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The container would destroy the pleasant smell, which is the whole purpose of keeping wine for sprinkling.

steps.title: The worry about a mishap is itself a dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that whether we worry about a mishap from keeping impure תרומה is itself argued about by the תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the mishap itself is a dispute of תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a side comment. The concern for a mishap, which it just relied on, is not agreed on by everyone. This line sets up the source that shows the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא assumed we worry about a mishap with wine. Now it admits that some תנאים do not share this worry. The next step brings the ברייתא that proves it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among the תנאים

phrases.english: And the mishap itself is a dispute of Tannaim.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַקָּלָה עַצְמָהּ, תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the oil/wine discussion to show that the mishap concern itself is debated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether we worry about a mishap from keeping impure תרומה is a dispute between תנאים.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל on a barrel of impure תרומה wine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: for a barrel of impure תרומה wine, בית שמאי say pour it out all at once, and בית הלל say use it for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: a barrel of תרומה wine that became impure. בית שמאי say: it should be poured out all at once. בית הלל say: it should be made into sprinkling wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the dispute. בית שמאי want the impure wine thrown away right now, while בית הלל let it be kept for sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי worry about a mishap, so they say pour it out. בית הלל do not worry, so they allow keeping it until it ages and using it for sprinkling. This proves the claim of Step 34.

keyTerms.meaning: It should be poured out all at once
It should be made into sprinkling wine

steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל are not saying to sprinkle new wine right away. The idea, as some explain it, is to wait until it ages and then use it for sprinkling.

phrases.english: As it was taught: a barrel of wine
of terumah that became impure,
Beit Shammai say: it should be poured out all at once,
phrases.notes: They fear a mishap if it is kept.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: it should be made into sprinkling wine.
phrases.notes: They are not concerned about a mishap.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: חָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנִּטְמֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the claim in Step 34.
steps.raayaObject: That the mishap concern is a dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute of בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.whyThisMatters: The earlier reasoning in Steps 29 to 33 follows בית שמאי's concern, so it is not the only view.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי decides: field or house
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי offers a middle path. If the barrel is in the field, pour it out. If it is in the house, use it for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said: I will decide. In the field, it should be poured out all at once. In the house, it should be made into sprinkling wine.
steps.whatsHappening: A later תנא tries to settle the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל. He splits the cases by where the barrel is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the field, the impurity may be forgotten by the time the wine is brought home, so there is a risk of a mishap and it must be poured out. In the house it can be used right away, so there is no risk and it may be kept for sprinkling.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said:
I will decide:
In the field, it should be poured out all at once,
phrases.notes: The impurity may be forgotten by the time it is brought home.

phrases.english: in the house, it should be made into sprinkling wine.
phrases.notes: It can be used right away, so there is no risk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אֲנִי אַכְרִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a compromise between the two views of Step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where a mishap is likely (field), pour it out. Where it is not (house), keep it for sprinkling.

steps.title: Another version: new or old wine
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי split it differently. New wine should be poured out, and old wine may be used for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: with new wine, it should be poured out all at once. With old wine, it should be made into sprinkling wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of how רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי decided. This time the split depends on whether the wine is new or old.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New wine would have to wait a long time to age, and in that time someone may forget and drink it, so pour it out. Old wine is ready for sprinkling now, so there is no long wait and no risk. This matches the new-wine idea from Step 27.

phrases.english: Some say:
with new wine, it should be poured out all at once,
phrases.notes: It would need a long time to age, which risks a mishap.

phrases.english: with old wine, it should be made into sprinkling wine.
phrases.notes: It can be used for sprinkling right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: בְּחָדָשׁ תִּשָּׁפֵךְ חֲבָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the compromise in Step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: New impure wine is poured out. Old impure wine may be kept for sprinkling.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי follow one idea: pour out the wine when keeping it risks a mishap, and allow sprinkling when it does not.

steps.title: The others begin to respond to him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins the response others gave to רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי. Their words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. It opens a reply to רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's decision, and the content of the reply comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ברייתא only introduces the speakers' response to his attempt to decide the dispute. We should wait for the next passage to see exactly what they object to.

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: Introduces a response that continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a response to the compromise given in Steps 36 and 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's attempt to decide between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The content of the response appears on the next amud. This line only introduces it.
